selector.rationale: Patient presented with acute abdominal pain, fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, and had a perforated appendix with peritonism, which are all consistent with sepsis due to a perforated viscus.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphadenopathy was present, it was not the primary cause of the patient's acute presentation.

rejected.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
rejected.why: Although the patient had a history of prostate cancer, the current presentation was more consistent with an acute abdominal process rather than metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
rejected.why: While the patient had pulmonary consolidation and required ventilation, ARDS was not the primary diagnosis, but rather a complication of the sepsis.
